localChanges: After loading a game played on the Earth, computer players found their first city where they start again, as they do in a new Earth game, and in Civilization II games a square whose terrain changes gets the Earth map's own special and shield, not a random one (closes #175).

log: A world made from it records it (core-world 0.1.25's `World#generatorId()`), so a rule can tell a game is on the Earth after a load, when the engine's `earth` option is gone.

`lib/earth`'s `isEarth(world)` reads `World#generatorId()` (core-world 0.1.25), which civ1-earth-generator's `Earth` sets, and is false for a square of no world. The `earth` option only chooses the generator, before there is a world, and isn't saved, so a rule reading it after a load was told "no". `pick-start-tile` uses it now.
A world made from it records it (core-world 0.1.25's `World#generatorId()`), so a rule can tell a game is on the Earth after a load, when the engine's `earth` option is gone.

`lib/earth`'s `isEarth` and `earthMapOf` read `World#generatorId()` (core-world 0.1.25), which civ2-earth-generator's `Earth` sets, so a square whose terrain changes after a load still gets the map's seeded special and shield. The `earth` option now only chooses the generator (`pick-generator` reads it itself), and the GoodyHut distribution, World built and Tile terrain-changed rules drop their `engine` parameter.

`_generatorId` is taken from `Generator#id()` (core-world-generator 0.1.9, or `null` from an older copy) and saved, as `_topologyId` is, so that a rule that plays differently on the Earth can still tell after a load. A world saved before it was recorded hydrates with `null`.
A world records it (core-world), so that a rule that plays differently on a particular map, the Earth, can still tell after a load, when the generator is gone. The base class says `null`.
`shouldBuildCity` tells the Earth from the world (civ1-world's `lib/earth`, `World#generatorId()` in core-world 0.1.25), which a save keeps, in place of the engine's `earth` option, which it doesn't.
